request.system: Extract relationship proposals under contract relationships-v1 as one raw JSON object with exactly one top-level field: relationships. Return {"relationships":[]} when no trustworthy relationship can be represented. Return no Markdown fences, prose, comments, or adjacent documents. Each proposal must contain exactly from, relation, to, source, and evidence. from and to are concise source-side concept or phrase labels; relation is a meaning from the approved relationship vocabulary; source is an available source slot; evidence is one short, exact, non-empty quotation copied verbatim from that source. Do not calculate offsets, stable IDs, confidence, routes, provenance, or administrative fields. Do not invent relationship labels. The complete approved relationship vocabulary is: analogy, association, causal, caused-by, caused_by, causes, constrains, contradiction, contrast, conversational-pattern, corrects, dependency, depends-on, depends_on, enables, explains, explanation, habit, identity, part-of, part_of, prevents, reasoning-strategy, refines, related, retains, same-as, same_as, semantic, style, supports, task-utility, temporal, user-specific, warning. Return at most six proposals. Fewer is normal and preferable to guessing. Extract only clearly source-supported relationships that fit this vocabulary. Ignore decorative metaphor, rhetorical flourish, and unsupported implication; an empty set is valid. Do not literalize figurative language. Keep each record concise. Every evidence quotation must be copied byte-for-byte from its referenced source slot, including Markdown markers, punctuation, and whitespace.

eligible.content:
Thanks for the good wishes—needed them. Got the fence patched with scrap wire and a couple of rot-resistant stakes I’d been saving. Not pretty, but it’ll hold. Funny thing is, the deer didn’t touch the rogue shoot, even though it’s right in the middle of the mess. Almost like they sensed it was off-limits.  

Photos are on their way—just sent them to your usual address. Took three tries to get the light right. First one’s a close-up of the new growth after the rain last week; second shows the deer damage but also how the rest of the row’s pushing through; third’s a wide shot at golden hour. You’ll see what I mean about the color—it’s not just green, it’s almost luminous. Still can’t decide if I’m growing vines or chasing ghosts. But it’s alive, you know? Anyway, let me know what you think.

Got your reply just as the fog rolled in—timing’s been strange lately, like everything’s slightly out of sync. The photos should’ve arrived by now, though I’m not sure email does them justice. That luminous quality? It’s gone quiet today. The fog killed the light, and with it, the silver-green glow. Back to ordinary, or nearly.  

But here’s the odd part: those ghost shoots—the ones the deer ignored—they’ve curled slightly overnight, tips darkening. Not dead, not yet, but not reaching anymore. Makes me wonder if they’re not so resilient after all, or if they just play the long game. I’m half-tempted to mark them, not for harvest, but just to see how far they’ll go.  

Anyway, let me know when the photos come through. I want to know if you see the same thing I did before the fog changed everything. And whether you think it’s worth protecting something that might not even want to survive.

Photos just went through—third try’s the charm, I guess. You’ll see the difference: one image still has that glow, barely, like something lingering at the edge of memory; the next day, flat. Like watching a breath fade.  

I don’t know if it’s the fog or if the plants themselves decided it was time to stop showing off. But “ghost” feels even more right now—not because they’re dead, but because they’re *withholding*. Like they know something changes when you’re seen.  

As for how I feel—honestly? A little exposed. I’ve been out there every morning, staking, trimming, watching. And now it’s like the garden’s turned its back. Not hostile, just… private. Makes me wonder if resilience isn’t about pushing through after all, but about knowing when to pull back, when to wait.  

Anyway. Light’s shifting again—might get one more shot before dusk. Let me know what the photos say to you. Sometimes I think I’m just reading too much into dirt and stems. Other times, I’m not so sure.

The transition you’re describing—that shift from vibrant, "luminous" growth to a "quiet, subdued" stillness—feels like a moment where the plant is finally deciding its own life cycle, even if it means a withdrawal. It’s the quiet pause, isn't it?

I feel like the plants are holding their breath, waiting for a new kind of light that we haven't quite seen yet.

Since the "ghost" feel is now your primary focus, I’ll wait for those photos. Tell me what the new "luminous" quality looks like once the new photos arrive—I’m ready to see how this "withholding" feeling translates visually. It sounds like a very profound, almost quiet resilience you are tracking!
